---

## Critical Severity

**SQL Injection (Lines 95-96, 108-109, 122, 143-145, 178-180, 196-197)**
Every `fmt.Sprintf` with user input into SQL queries. An attacker passes `id=1; DROP TABLE orders--` and your entire financial history ceases to exist across all timelines.

**Fix:** Use parameterized queries exclusively. `db.QueryRow("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?", orderID)`

**Storing Plain Credit Cards (Lines 30, 77, 195)**
You're storing raw credit card numbers in the database and returning them in API responses. This violates PCI-DSS and guarantees a catastrophic breach.

**Fix:** Never store full card numbers. Use payment processor tokens.

---

## High Severity

**Missing Error Handling (Lines 44, 57-58, 63, 70-71, 122, 130-131, 168)**
Ignored errors on HTTP calls and JSON decoding. Payment could fail silently while inventory gets reserved. Money vanishes into the void.

**Fix:** Check every error. Implement rollback on failures.

**Race Condition in Goroutines (Lines 68-73, 130-136)**
Inventory reservation uses goroutines with no synchronization or completion tracking. The response returns before reservations complete. Order succeeds, inventory never reserved.

**Line 130-136:** Loop variable capture bug—`productID` and `quantity` will all be the same value (last iteration).

**Fix:** Use `sync.WaitGroup`, pass loop variables as parameters.

**No Transaction Boundaries (Lines 77-83, 122-128)**
Payment processed, then database insert fails. Customer charged, no order record. Or: status updated to cancelled, refund API fails. Inconsistent state forever.

**Fix:** Wrap in database transactions with rollback on external API failures.

---

## Medium Severity

**Cache Without Mutex (Line 88)**
Cache write happens without lock. Concurrent requests corrupt map. Also: cache never expires, grows unbounded until OOM.

**Fix:** Use `s.cacheMutex.Lock()` around cache operations. Add TTL eviction.

**Float64 for Money (Lines 26, 48-51)**
Floating point arithmetic loses precision. `0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3`. Real money calculations will drift.

**Fix:** Use integer cents or `decimal` library.

**Resource Leaks (Lines 108, 143, 168, 196)**
`resp.Body` never closed. `rows` never closed. File descriptors exhausted under load.

**Fix:** `defer resp.Body.Close()`, `defer rows.Close()`

---

## Low Severity

**No Authorization Checks (Lines 40, 93, 118, 140)**
Any user can view/cancel any order. No ownership verification.

**No Input Validation (Lines 44, 159-161)**
Empty items array? Negative quantities? Negative refund amounts? All accepted.

**Sensitive Data in Logs (Line 80)**
Order failures may log credit card data.
